top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Bergen-Voss' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.

Road-specific control matters at Bergen-Voss. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 107 miles.
64ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At mile 60 of 107, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
At Bergen-Voss, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
6,890ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Bergen-Voss. Train it until it feels boring.
6,890ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Bergen-Voss. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 6,890ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 107 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Bergen-Voss’s 107 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Bergen-Voss. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Bergen-Voss rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 107 miles of mixed terrain in Bergen to Voss, Norway.
